citation_entries.sentence: The Chronicle of Edessa records for the year 513 of the Greeks: “And they destroyed the temple of the church of the Christians.”
A dispute exists over whether that church-destruction entry is original or was added later.
Still, that line is the oldest dated word about us, drawn from real archives.

raw_text: We can speak only to the outside records we hold: the city chronicle's flood line and Theodoret's tale of Jacob's prayer, and neither tells of our worship [[syr.quote.chronicle-flood-line]] [[syr.quote.theodoret-gnats]] [[as:paraphrase]]. The Chronicle of Edessa is a sixth-century compilation from the city archives, not an eyewitness record [[syr.quote.chronicle-flood-line]] [[as:paraphrase]]. The Chronicle of Edessa records for the year 513 of the Greeks: [[quote:syr.quote.chronicle-flood-line]] [[as:paraphrase]]. A dispute exists over whether that church-destruction entry is original or was added later [[syr.quote.chronicle-flood-line]] [[syr.dw.corpus-and-its-edges]] [[as:paraphrase]]. Still, that line is the oldest dated word about us, drawn from real archives [[syr.dw.corpus-and-its-edges]] [[as:paraphrase]]. Theodoret, writing about a century later, tells that Jacob of Nisibis called down only mosquitoes and gnats on the besieging Persians [[syr.quote.theodoret-gnats]] [[as:paraphrase]]. That is hagiographic legend, not a verified event, and the siege year may be 338, 346, or 350 [[syr.quote.theodoret-gnats]] [[as:paraphrase]].
